017package org.apache.juneau.commons.beanquery;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.Shorts.*;
020
021import java.time.*;
022
023/**
024 * The per-column value type that governs which search operators apply to a column and how a bare (no leading
025 * {@code $}) pattern token is interpreted.
026 *
027 * <p>
028 * A column's value type selects both the operator set offered for that column
029 * ({@link SearchOperatorSet#forType(SearchType)}) and the leaf-comparison semantics a context applies.  The lowercase
030 * {@link #wire() wire token} is the stable external spelling.  {@link #bareHelp()} is a fixed, one-sentence
031 * explanation of bare-token behavior intended for display in a search-bar popover.
032 *
033 * <h5 class='section'>Bare-token behavior per type:</h5>
034 * <ul>
035 *    <li>{@link #TEXT} / {@link #ID} &mdash; case-insensitive substring (same idea as {@code $contains}).
036 *    <li>{@link #VERSION} &mdash; dotted-tuple prefix.
037 *    <li>{@link #NUMERIC} / {@link #TIMESTAMP} / {@link #ENUM} / {@link #BOOLEAN} &mdash; exact equality.
038 * </ul>
039 *
040 * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
041 * <p class='bjava'>
042 *    String <jv>help</jv> = SearchType.VERSION.<jsm>bareHelp</jsm>();
043 *    <jc>// help == "Matches any version starting with this prefix, e.g. 250 matches 250.1 and 250.2.3."</jc>
044 * </p>
045 *
046 * <h5 class='section'>Example (typing a literal):</h5>
047 * <p class='bjava'>
048 *    <jc>// Type a literal the same way for every engine, so a bad value is BAD_VALUE (400) everywhere.</jc>
049 *    Object <jv>v</jv> = SearchType.<jsf>NUMERIC</jsf>.<jsm>parse</jsm>(<js>"42"</js>);  <jc>// BigDecimal("42")</jc>
050 * </p>
051 *
052 * @since 10.0.0
053 */
054public enum SearchType {
055
056   /** Free text.  Bare token is a case-insensitive substring match. */
057   TEXT("text", "Matches any value containing this text (case-insensitive). Use $eq(...) for an exact, case-sensitive match."),
058
059   /** An id-like string (identifiers, keys).  Bare token is a case-insensitive substring match, same as {@link #TEXT}. */
060   ID("id", "Matches any value containing this text (case-insensitive). Use $eq(...) for an exact, case-sensitive match."),
061
062   /** A number.  Bare token is exact equality; supports the ordered operators. */
063   NUMERIC("numeric", "Matches a number exactly. Use $gt / $gte / $lt / $lte / $between for a range, or a duration such as -24h or -PT24H (= -86400000 ms)."),
064
065   /** A dotted version tuple (e.g. {@code 10.0.0}).  Bare token is a dotted-tuple prefix; supports the ordered operators and {@code $prefix}. */
066   VERSION("version", "Matches any version starting with this prefix, e.g. 250 matches 250.1 and 250.2.3."),
067
068   /**
069    * An instant/timestamp.  Bare token is exact equality; supports the ordered operators.
070    *
071    * <p>
072    * <b>Offset advice:</b> a value with an explicit offset ({@code 2026-09-30T12:00:00Z},
073    * {@code 2026-09-30T12:00:00-04:00}) always denotes one absolute instant.  The local forms (a date-time without an
074    * offset, or a bare date) have no zone: in-memory matching treats them as UTC, while a SQL engine hands them to the
075    * database, which interprets them in the <i>session</i> time zone.  The two can therefore disagree, so prefer the
076    * offset forms (or epoch milliseconds, which are always UTC) in any search that must behave identically everywhere.
077    * See {@link #parse(String)}.
078    */
079   TIMESTAMP("timestamp", "Matches an exact instant; a bare date means UTC midnight exactly, so for a whole day use $between(d, d+1). Also accepts a duration such as -24h or -PT24H, relative to the request time."),
080
081   /** A one-of enumerated value.  Bare token is a case-insensitive exact match. */
082   ENUM("enum", "Matches one value exactly, case-insensitive."),
083
084   /** A boolean.  Bare token is exact equality; supports only {@code $eq}/{@code $ne}. */
085   BOOLEAN("boolean", "Matches true or false exactly.");
086
087   private final String wire;
088   private final String bareHelp;
089
090   SearchType(String wire, String bareHelp) {
091      this.wire = wire;
092      this.bareHelp = bareHelp;
093   }
094
095   /**
096    * Returns the lowercase wire token for this type (e.g. {@code "text"}).
097    *
098    * @return The wire token.
099    */
100   public String wire() {
101      return wire;
102   }
103
104   /**
105    * Returns a fixed, one-sentence explanation of what a bare (no leading {@code $}) token means for a column of
106    * this type, intended for display in a search-bar popover.
107    *
108    * @return The help string.  Never <jk>null</jk> or blank.
109    */
110   public String bareHelp() {
111      return bareHelp;
112   }
113
114   /**
115    * Resolves a wire token back to its {@link SearchType}.
116    *
117    * @param wire The lowercase wire token (case-insensitive).  Can be <jk>null</jk>.
118    * @return The matching type, or <jk>null</jk> if {@code wire} is <jk>null</jk>, blank, or unrecognized.
119    */
120   public static SearchType fromWire(String wire) {
121      if (wire == null)
122         return null;
123      var w = wire.trim();
124      for (var t : values())
125         if (eqic(t.wire, w))
126            return t;
127      return null;
128   }
129
130   /**
131    * Parses a decoded literal (quotes stripped, escapes undone) into this type's Java representation.
132    *
133    * <p>
134    * {@link #NUMERIC} parses to {@link java.math.BigDecimal}; {@link #BOOLEAN} to {@link Boolean}
135    * (case-insensitive {@code true}/{@code false}); {@link #TIMESTAMP} to {@link java.time.OffsetDateTime} (has an
136    * offset), {@link java.time.LocalDateTime} (no offset), {@link java.time.LocalDate} (date only), or, for a bare
137    * integer, an {@link java.time.OffsetDateTime} at UTC built from epoch milliseconds (optional leading {@code -}; no
138    * {@code +}).  The local forms carry no zone - see the offset advice on {@link #TIMESTAMP}.  {@link #TEXT}, {@link #ID},
139    * {@link #ENUM} and {@link #VERSION} are returned unchanged (never <jk>null</jk>; a <jk>null</jk> {@code value}
140    * becomes {@code ""}).
141    *
142    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
143    * <p class='bjava'>
144    *    BigDecimal <jv>n</jv> = (BigDecimal)SearchType.<jsf>NUMERIC</jsf>.<jsm>parse</jsm>(<js>"-3.5"</js>);
145    * </p>
146    *
147    * @param value The decoded literal text, or <jk>null</jk> (treated as empty).
148    * @return The parsed value.
149    * @throws BeanQuerySyntaxException (code {@link BeanQuerySyntaxException.Code#BAD_VALUE BAD_VALUE}) If
150    *    {@code value} does not parse for this type ({@link #NUMERIC}, {@link #BOOLEAN} or {@link #TIMESTAMP} only).
151    * @since 10.0.0
152    */
153   public Object parse(String value) {
154      return ValueParse.parse(this, value);
155   }
156
157   /**
158    * Parses a decoded literal like {@link #parse(String)}, resolving a relative-duration literal against
159    * {@code requestTime} instead of the current instant.
160    *
161    * <p>
162    * A relative-duration literal is {@code [+-]<n>(ms|s|m|h|d)} (lowercase units only), e.g. {@code -24h}, or a signed ISO-8601 duration ({@code PT24H}, {@code -PT24H},
163    * {@code +PT30M}, {@code P1D}) with identical semantics (only one leading sign; {@code PT-1H}, years, months and
164    * weeks are {@code BAD_VALUE}).  For
165    * {@link #NUMERIC} it parses to the signed amount in milliseconds (a {@link java.math.BigDecimal}; "now" is never
166    * involved).  For {@link #TIMESTAMP} it parses to {@code requestTime} plus the signed amount, as an
167    * {@link java.time.OffsetDateTime} at UTC.  A bare signed number such as {@code -5} is never a duration, and a total that overflows a {@code long} (for
168    * {@link #TIMESTAMP}, after adding {@code requestTime}'s epoch milliseconds) is {@code BAD_VALUE}.  On
169    * {@link #BOOLEAN} a duration is {@code BAD_VALUE}; {@link #TEXT}, {@link #ID}, {@link #ENUM} and {@link #VERSION}
170    * are untyped and keep the text literally.  Every
171    * other literal shape parses exactly as in {@link #parse(String)}; {@link #parse(String)} itself delegates here
172    * with {@link Instant#now()}.
173    *
174    * <h5 class='section'>Example:</h5>
175    * <p class='bjava'>
176    *    Instant <jv>now</jv> = Instant.<jsm>parse</jsm>(<js>"2026-09-30T12:00:00Z"</js>);
177    *    Object <jv>yesterday</jv> = SearchType.<jsf>TIMESTAMP</jsf>.<jsm>parse</jsm>(<js>"-24h"</js>, <jv>now</jv>);  <jc>// 2026-09-29T12:00Z</jc>
178    *    Object <jv>ms</jv> = SearchType.<jsf>NUMERIC</jsf>.<jsm>parse</jsm>(<js>"-24h"</js>, <jv>now</jv>);  <jc>// BigDecimal("-86400000")</jc>
179    * </p>
180    *
181    * @param value The decoded literal text, or <jk>null</jk> (treated as empty).
182    * @param requestTime The instant a relative-duration {@link #TIMESTAMP} literal resolves against.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
183    * @return The parsed value.
184    * @throws BeanQuerySyntaxException (code {@link BeanQuerySyntaxException.Code#BAD_VALUE BAD_VALUE}) If
185    *    {@code value} does not parse for this type ({@link #NUMERIC}, {@link #BOOLEAN} or {@link #TIMESTAMP} only).
186    * @since 10.0.0
187    */
188   public Object parse(String value, Instant requestTime) {
189      return ValueParse.parse(this, value, reqnn("requestTime", requestTime));
190   }
191}
